### Corrections & Patterns to Avoid

Architecture and technology choices from past sessions.

- [sift] Roadmap items already completed as of v0.1.3: parallel startup, input validation, streaming output, retry with backoff, fuzz testing, search cache, property tests, release automation, binary size tracking
- [Cortex hook stdin schemas] Claude Code hooks send JSON on stdin. Common fields: session_id, transcript_path, cwd, permission_mode, hook_event_name. Optional: agent_id, agent_type (for subagents)
- [Cortex hook stdin schemas] PostToolUse stdin adds: tool_name (string), tool_input (object, schema varies by tool), tool_response (object), tool_use_id. Matcher matches on tool_name. MCP tools use full name like 'mcp__sift__sift_remember'
- [Cortex hook stdin schemas] Stop stdin adds: stop_hook_active (bool, true if already continuing from stop hook — check to prevent infinite loops), last_assistant_message (string, Claude's final response text)
- [Cortex hook stdin schemas] PostCompact stdin adds: trigger ('manual' | 'auto'), compact_summary (string, the conversation summary generated by compaction). PostCompact has NO decision control — purely observational
- [Cortex hook stdin schemas] Exit code 0 = success (stdout parsed for JSON), exit code 2 = blocking error (stderr fed to Claude), any other = non-blocking error. For PostToolUse, output JSON can have decision/reason/additionalContext fields
- [Cortex hook stdin schemas] Hook config in settings.json: hooks.EventName is array of { matcher?: string, hooks: [{ type: 'command', command: string, timeout?: number }] }. Matcher supports regex-like patterns (Edit|Write|Bash)

- [Cortex automated memory system] Hot path uses three Claude Code hooks: PostToolUse (write tools only), Stop (last_assistant_message), and PostCompact (compact_summary — pre-distilled session knowledge for free)
- [Cortex automated memory system] Cold path consolidation has 5 phases: (1) episode processing — rule-based entity/fact extraction, (2) deduplication — exact text + embedding cosine >0.92, (3) episodic→semantic promotion — access count + age threshold, (4) skill extraction — repeated patterns → procedural knowledge, (5) decay & pruning — utility-per-token scoring
- [Cortex automated memory system] Three memory tiers: episodic (raw, session-tagged), semantic (consolidated facts, high confidence), procedural (learned skills, never auto-deleted)
- [Cortex automated memory system] Retrieval-dependent strengthening: access_log table tracks every recall hit, access_count on observations, enhanced scoring formula with retrieval_boost = 1 + 0.15 * ln(1 + access_count)
- [Cortex automated memory system] Utility-per-token scoring from PlugMem: utility = (relevance * access_freq * confidence) / max(1, token_count/50) — quality over quantity

Phase 2 = consolidation.rs + skills table + sift_consolidate MCP tool. Phase 3 = daemon loop + HTTP endpoints + entity resolution + spreading activation
- [Cortex automated memory system] PLAN.md written at /Users/rjow/sift/PLAN.md with full implementation details
- [sift memory design] Relation-only entities (like 'Rust' and 'Claude Code' with 0 observations but active incoming relations) serve as structural anchors in the knowledge graph. sift_prune correctly preserves these.
- [sift memory design] Some duplication exists between 'sift MCP config' and 'MCP protocol' entities (config precedence, /mcp retry behavior stored in both). A consolidation pass could deduplicate these.
- [sift memory design] Bi-temporal modeling (observed_at vs valid_from/valid_until) is the standout design choice — separating 'when the agent learned it' from 'when the fact was true' enables historical queries and proper fact supersession without losing audit history. Pattern originates from Snodgrass's temporal databases, recently popularized by Zep/Graphiti.
- [sift memory design] Memory observations share the same hybrid search engine as file search via URI scheme (memory:// vs file://). This means memory search automatically benefits from core search improvements (caching, scoring, RRF tuning) without duplicating infrastructure.
- [sift memory design] Memory recall uses alpha=0.7 (70% vector, 30% keyword) vs the default for files — heavier vector weight makes sense because memory observations are short natural-language sentences where semantic similarity matters more than exact keyword matching.
- [sift memory design] sift_forget soft-deletes observations by setting valid_until, but leaves the parent entity behind. Over time this creates ghost entities with 0 visible observations. sift_forget_entity and sift_prune were added to address this.
- [sift memory design] sift_prune's safety check: entities with 0 observations but active relations (like 'Rust' being a target of Raymond 'prefers' Rust) are preserved. The NOT EXISTS check on the relations table prevents pruning entities that are still part of the knowledge graph structure.
- [rusqlite patterns] MappedRows borrows Statement, so you can't return the collected result as the final expression of a block where Statement is a local. Fix: bind the result to a named variable (let x = stmt.query_map(...)?.collect(); x) before the block ends.
- [rusqlite patterns] NOT EXISTS subqueries are preferred over LEFT JOIN ... IS NULL for anti-joins that check multiple tables simultaneously. NOT EXISTS also short-circuits on the first matching row, making it generally faster in SQLite.
- [MCP protocol] MCP servers communicate over stdio using a 3-step JSON-RPC handshake: (1) client sends initialize request, (2) server responds with capabilities, (3) client sends initialized notification. Any stdout contamination (non-JSON-RPC output) breaks the protocol.
- [MCP protocol] ~/.claude/settings.json does NOT support mcpServers — only ~/.claude.json does. Global MCP servers go in ~/.claude.json (user scope). Project-level .mcp.json is shared by any tool that reads it (Cursor, Claude Code), which creates contention when multiple clients spawn the same server against shared state like SQLite databases.
- [MCP protocol] The `/mcp` slash command only retries stale connections — it does not re-read config. A full Claude Code restart is required after MCP config changes.
- [sift MCP config] The sift MCP server must be configured at user scope in ~/.claude.json (not ~/.claude/settings.json, which ignores mcpServers). Use `claude mcp add -s user` to set it up.
- [sift MCP config] The correct command is `/opt/homebrew/bin/sift mcp` with env ORT_DYLIB_PATH=/Users/rjow/.sift/models/ort/libonnxruntime.dylib. Always use the absolute path to the release binary.
- [sift MCP config] The project-level ~/sift/.mcp.json was removed to prevent Cursor from spawning a competing sift MCP instance that locks the SQLite databases (fts5.db, metadata.db).
